notes: §1985:XIII.3.6.3 SR1: 'Literal-1 must be a two-character nonnumeric literal.' BindCodeClause refuses a literal whose class is not alphanumeric and, at 85, an identifier operand (the 2002 form); Screen85CodeLiteral refuses at DialectLevel < 2002 a literal whose characters are not two (COBOL2713, the witness: CODE "A"). Probes at --std 85 (classes b, c, d): CODE "AB" and CODE "A""" compile and write AB / A" in the first two positions of each line (§1985:XIII.3.6.4 GR1); "ABC", "" (also COBOL0900), 12, N"AB", WS-C, a bare CODE, CODE twice (COBOL2423), and the 2002 forms CODE IS, X"4142" and "A" & "B" (COBOL0900) are refused. DEFECT: every figurative constant is refused as 'not an alphanumeric literal', but §1985:IV.4.2.2.2.3 says 'A figurative constant may be used whenever 'literal' appears in a format with the following exceptions' and excepts only a numeric-restricted literal, and its rule (3) gives ALL literal unassociated 'the length of the literal', so CODE ALL "AB" is a two-character nonnumeric value the 1985 text admits (and, read as associated with GR1's two positions, CODE SPACE too). kb/Work PB5475 holds the defect (code read: coderead-85/out-read4/rd-01.json).

next.reason: 1985: "Literal-1 must be a two-character nonnumeric literal."; 2023: "Literal-1 shall be an alphanumeric literal.". 2023 drops the two-character length requirement; alphanumeric literals of other lengths are now accepted in the CODE clause.
